st: Divide the beef into 4 equal balls. Press each into a patty about 4 inches wide, with a small dimple in the center.
Season both sides with the salt and pepper just before cooking.
Heat a cast iron skillet or grill over medium-high heat.
Cook the patties for 4 minutes without pressing down. Flip them.
Cook 4 more minutes until they reach 160°F (71°C). Add a cheese slice in the last minute and cover to melt.
Spread the butter on the buns and toast them in the pan for 1 minute.
Build the burgers with lettuce, patty and cheese, tomato, onion and pickles.
Add ketchup and mustard and serve.
Boil the macaroni in well-salted water for 2 minutes less than the package says. Drain.
Heat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter a 9x13-inch dish.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly pour in the warm milk, whisking nonstop. Cook 5 minutes until thick enough to coat a spoon.
Take the pot off the heat. Stir in [[2.5 cups]] of the cheese, the salt, pepper and mustard powder until smooth.
Fold in the macaroni and pour into the dish.
Top with the rest of the cheese and the breadcrumbs.
Bake for 20 minutes until bubbly and golden. Rest 5 minutes.
Put the chicken in a bowl or bag with the buttermilk and [[2 tsp]] salt. Turn to coat.
Marinate in the fridge for at least [[4 hours]] or overnight.
Mix the flour, paprika, garlic powder, pepper, cayenne and [[1 tsp]] salt in a wide dish.
Lift each piece from the buttermilk, letting extra drip off, and press into the flour mixture until well coated.
Let the coated chicken rest on a rack for [[15 minutes]] so the coating sticks.
Heat the oil in a deep heavy pot to 325°F (165°C).
Fry in batches, 4 pieces at a time, for 12 to 15 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and the thickest part reaches 165°F (74°C).
Drain on a rack and rest 5 minutes before serving.
Heat the oven to 275°F (135°C). Remove the thin membrane from the back of the ribs by pulling it with a paper towel.
Mix the sugar, paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, salt and pepper into a rub.
Rub it all over the ribs on both sides.
Wrap the ribs tightly in foil and place on a baking sheet.
Bake for 2 hours 30 minutes until the meat is very tender and the pork reaches at least 190°F (88°C) for pulling-tender texture.
Unwrap and brush the ribs with half the BBQ sauce.
Broil or grill for 5 minutes until the sauce is sticky. Brush with more sauce.
Rest 10 minutes and cut between the bones.
Pat the wings very dry with paper towels.
Toss with the baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Put a rack on a baking sheet and arrange the wings on it.
Bake for 25 minutes, turn, and bake 20 more minutes until crisp and golden. The wings must reach 165°F (74°C).
Whisk the hot sauce and melted butter together in a large bowl.
Add the hot wings and toss to coat.
Serve right away with celery sticks and blue cheese dressing.
Cook the bacon in a large pot over medium heat for 7 minutes until crisp. Remove and set aside.
Add the butter, onion and celery to the bacon fat. Cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the reserved clam juice, bottled clam juice and potatoes. Add the thyme.
Simmer for 15 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Stir in the cream, clams, salt and pepper. Warm gently for 5 minutes without boiling.
Remove the thyme stems, taste, and serve topped with the bacon.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef for 10 minutes, breaking it up, until no pink remains.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, broth and salt. Bring to a boil.
Lower the heat, cover partly, and simmer for 1 hour.
Add the beans and simmer 15 more minutes until thick.
Taste and adjust salt. Serve hot.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Whisk the milk, egg and [[3 tbsp]] melted butter in a second bowl.
Pour the wet mix into the dry and stir just until combined. Small lumps are fine.
Rest the batter for [[5 minutes]].
Heat a skillet over medium heat and rub with butter.
Pour [[0.25 cup]] batter per pancake. Cook until bubbles form and burst, about 2 minutes.
Flip and cook 1 to 2 minutes until golden.
Stack and serve warm with butter and maple syrup.

ing: tart, such as Granny Smith, peeled and sliced
st: Mix the flour and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cut in the butter with your fingers until pea-sized crumbs form.
Add the ice water a spoonful at a time until the dough just holds together. Divide in two, flatten, wrap, and chill for [[1 hour]].
Toss the apples with [[0.75 cup]] sugar, the cinnamon, lemon juice, cornstarch and [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Roll one dough disc to a 12-inch round and fit into a 9-inch pie dish.
Pile in the apples. Roll out the second disc and lay over the top.
Trim, crimp the edge, cut 5 slits in the top, brush with egg and sprinkle with [[1 tbsp]] sugar.
Bake for 20 minutes, then lower to 375°F (190°C) and bake 40 minutes more until golden and bubbling.
Cool for at least [[2 hours]] so the filling sets.
Bring the water to a simmer in a pot.
Add the hot dogs and heat for 5 minutes, until hot all the way through.
Or grill them over medium heat for 6 minutes, turning, until browned.
Warm the buns in the oven at 300°F (150°C) for 3 minutes.
Place each hot dog in a bun.
Add the mustard and ketchup.
Top with the onion and relish. Serve right away.
Put the ketchup, brown sugar, vinegar and molasses in a saucepan.
Add the Worcestershire, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, pepper and salt.
Whisk everything together until smooth.
Bring to a gentle bubble over medium heat.
Lower the heat and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring often, until thick.
Taste and adjust salt or sugar if you like.
Cool and store in a jar in the fridge for up to 2 weeks.
Whisk the mayonnaise and sour cream in a bowl until smooth.
Slowly whisk in the buttermilk.
Add the garlic, dill, parsley and chives.
Stir in the onion powder, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Cover and chill for [[30 minutes]] so the flavors blend.
Taste and adjust the salt.
Thin with a splash of buttermilk if you want it pourable. Keep in the fridge up to 5 days.
Cut the butter into small pieces and put them in a small saucepan.
Melt the butter over low heat without browning it.
Whisk the hot sauce into the melted butter.
Add the vinegar and garlic powder.
Warm for 3 minutes, whisking, until smooth. Do not boil.
Add the Worcestershire if using and a pinch of salt.
Toss with hot wings or use as a dip. Rewarm gently if it separates.
